key_insight: RetireOPD shows that in agentic reinforcement learning, a privileged self-teacher is not always trustworthy, and its guidance is only useful at certain stages of training. The paper’s key idea is to make on-policy distillation self-retiring: use teacher supervision when it helps, then stop relying on it when it becomes less beneficial.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of turning sparse trajectory-level RL rewards into dense token-level supervision for multi-turn agents, without being harmed by unreliable teacher signals or overusing guidance at the wrong training stage.
method: Train a self-teacher with privileged task information to provide dense on-policy token-level supervision.
Monitor when teacher guidance is helpful versus harmful across training stages.
Automatically retire or reduce teacher distillation when the student has learned enough or when supervision becomes unreliable.
impact: This makes RL training for agents more stable and efficient by avoiding blind reliance on a teacher. Practitioners can get better learning signals for long-horizon, multi-turn tasks while reducing noise and wasted supervision.
visual_elements: A two-stage training timeline showing 'guided distillation' transitioning to 'retired supervision'.
A comparison diagram of sparse trajectory reward vs dense token-level teacher signals.
A reliability curve showing teacher usefulness changing over training stages.
Icons for teacher, student, reward, and retirement/stop to illustrate the self-retiring mechanism.
paper_title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Yan Yu, Zhengxi Lu, Yizhou Liu, Yichen Pan, Aozhe Wang
